processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Ingots with nominal composition Fe-35Mn-17Al-5Cu (at.%) produced by melting high-purity (>99.9 %) raw materials in a vacuum induction furnace under an argon atmosphere.
Hot-rolled into plates with a thickness of 4 mm, subsequently cut into 10 × 5 × 2 mm3 samples using electrical discharge machining.
Solution treated at 1100 °C for 10 min under an argon atmosphere, followed by oil quenching (parent process proc_st-1100c-10min-oq).
Solution-treated samples aged at temperatures between 525 °C and 650 °C for 1, 3, 6 and 10 h, followed by water quenching; this sample is the 550 °C / 6 h aging condition of the 17Al alloy.

structures.overall_structure: After aging at 550 °C for 6 h the α matrix of the 17Al alloy had nearly fully transformed into β-Mn; in SE-SEM the matrix is essentially featureless and labelled β-Mn.

phases_present.morphology: essentially featureless transformed matrix (nearly complete α→β-Mn transformation)

measurement_conditions.other_conditions: Vickers microhardness measured with an HVS-1000 digital microhardness tester, load 9.8 N for 15 s; each sample repeatedly tested 5 times and hardness given as the average of 5 measurements; samples electrolytically polished with 10 % perchloric acid + 90 % ethanol.
Density measured by the Archimedes method.

characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Load 9.8 N for 15 s; each sample tested 5 times; hardness = average of 5 measurements; specimens electrolytically polished (10 % perchloric acid + 90 % ethanol)
characterization_methods.purpose: Measure the Vickers hardness of the aged 17Al samples to quantify aging hardening
characterization_methods.key_findings: The 17Al alloy aged at 550 °C for 6 h has a Vickers hardness of 792.9 ± 16.9 HV (Table 3).

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: ZEISS Sigma 300 SEM operated at 5 kV
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Electrolytically polished aged 17Al samples; SE imaging (Fig. 8)
characterization_methods.purpose: Identify the precipitation of secondary phases (α-Mn and β-Mn) in the aged samples and track the α→β-Mn transformation
characterization_methods.key_findings: For the 17Al alloy aged at 550 °C for 6 h the matrix appears essentially featureless and is labelled β-Mn (green), consistent with the nearly complete α→β-Mn transformation after 6 h at 550 °C.

unmapped_findings: Solution-treated 17Al baseline (parent solution-treatment state, 1100 °C/10 min + oil quench): Vickers hardness 259.8 ± 1.5 HV (Table 3, b0030). This is the parent state rather than the 550 °C/6 h aged sample.

The paper's intrinsic β-Mn hardness (12.2 ± 0.1 GPa) and SEM-EDS β-Mn composition (Mn 36.2, Al 16.3, Cu 2.6 at.%) for 17Al were measured on the hardest 17Al sample aged at 575 °C/6 h, not on this 550 °C/6 h sample (b0060, b0067).
Fracture toughness KIC = 6.6 MPa·m1/2 for the 17Al alloy was determined for the hardest sample (575 °C/6 h, 924.9 HV), not for this 550 °C/6 h sample (b0061).

Fig. 2(b) hardness contour map for 17Al shows the optimal ultra-high-hardness window mainly at 550–600 °C (b0038); the 550 °C hardness series rises most slowly at 1 h and does not reach the peak of the alloy.
